precepts.text: The first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
“Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us.” What ordinances? The subject has not changed: the scribes and Pharisees were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, saying salvation comes through sacrifice. Hebrews shows where those ordinances belong: “Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.”

The ordinances of divine service, the offerings and the worldly sanctuary, belonged to the first covenant. They did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us. Those are the ordinances Christ took out of the way and nailed to his cross, and verse 10 of the same chapter tells what they stood in and how long they were to last.

precepts.text: Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation: until the time of Christ, the time of transformation.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
The ordinances of the first covenant “stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.” Meats and drinks are the meat offerings and drink offerings. Divers washings: remember Matthew 15, when they complained, your disciples don't wash their hands. That's what we're talking about.

“carnal ordinances, imposed on them”: forced on the Israelites. “until the time of reformation”: until the time of Christ. Reformation means the time of transformation, which is when Christ came.

That is the handwriting of ordinances in Colossians 2:14. They were imposed only until Christ, and he blotted them out, “which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.” Going back to them is going backward.

precepts.text: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect. It could not make you perfect, because it was an animal. Christ is the perfection of that law; they refused to accept and understand that.
precepts.point: Blotting out the handwriting of ordinances that was against us, which was contrary to us, and took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross. The subject has not changed: they were beguiling Israel to go back to animal sacrifice, and they did not understand that animal sacrifice was a symbol of what Christ would do for us.

note.label: Deceived by Enticing Words: Colossians 2

precepts.why:
Certain sins called for certain sacrifices, and all of that was against us, because it could not make us perfect: “Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience.”

It couldn't make you that did the service perfect, the priest or the one giving the offering. Why? It was an animal: a goat, a lamb, an ox or a turtledove. It was only a figure for that time.

Christ is the perfection of that law. They refused to accept and understand that, and that's the initial problem Paul was dealing with in Colossians 2. That is why the handwriting of ordinances “was contrary to us”, and why he “took it out of the way, nailing it to his cross.”

precepts.text: Not by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us. He is the mediator of the new testament, as Moses was mediator when we came out of Egypt; and where a testament is, there must of necessity be the death of the testator. That is why Christ had to die: a testament is of force after men are dead, and while the testator lives it can still change.
precepts.point: The day of atonement: on the tenth day of the seventh month ye shall afflict your souls. Christ was that atonement.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building; Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.” His blood was given for atonement, and he died only once. Eternal redemption for whom? For us, the Israelites.

“For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” Without spot means blameless: he had no sin.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament”, just as Moses was the mediator for us when we came up out of Egypt, so “that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” That promise is ours if we believe.

“For where a testament is, there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.” For the testament to come to fruition and be valid, the testator had to die. That is why Christ had to die. “For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.” While a man is alive, his testament can still change. “Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.” Blood had to be spilled for the first covenant of animal sacrifice too. The yearly atonement of Leviticus 23:27 was fulfilled once for all in Christ’s own blood.

precepts.text: A figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices that could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience, because sin was in us since Adam; which stood only in meats and drinks, meat and drink offerings, and divers washings, baptisms, and carnal ordinances, traditions of the Pharisees, imposed until the time of reformation, when Christ came. This is an example of the works of the law.
precepts.point: If ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise. Romans 9:3-5: Paul's kinsmen according to the flesh, Israelites, to whom pertaineth the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises, whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came. The heirs are Israelites.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“But before faith came, we were kept under the law, shut up unto the faith which should afterwards be revealed.” Who was kept under the law? “Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law”. We were locked into that covenant until Christ came, died, and granted us liberty.

What was it we were kept under? Hebrews gives an example of the works of the law: “Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”. The sacrifices could not make him that did them perfect, because sin was already in us since Adam. So the animals had to be temporary.

“Which stood only in meats and drinks”: meat offerings and drink offerings. These are the works of the law read all through Galatians, in 2:16, 3:2, 3:5 and 3:10-11. “and divers washings”: baptisms. “and carnal ordinances”: the traditions of the Pharisees. “imposed on them until the time of reformation.” Forced upon them until the time of reformation, which is the faith that should afterwards be revealed, when Christ came and did away with all of it.

So “the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ”. The schoolmaster was sacrifice. The sacrificing of animals was a foreshadowing of Christ's death, preparing us for his body. It was temporary, because we grew weary and rebellious behind it and would all have been condemned through it. “But after that faith is come, we are no longer under a schoolmaster”: no longer under the law of sacrifice.

precepts.text: For this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance. Who was under the first testament? Israel. Nail in the coffin.
precepts.point: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years; I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. Colossians 2:16: let no man judge you in meat or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. Ezekiel 45:17 answers both: it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings, and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths, and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and the Pharisees, whose bread and butter was people bringing animals, were trying to win the churches back to temple law, saying to hell with what Christ did. If you need an animal, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“But when the fulness of the time was come”, the time appointed of the Father, “God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.” Who did Christ come to redeem? Them that were under the law. The we is the same we of chapter 3 that were kept under the law, and the adoption pertains to Israel.

Hebrews is the nail in the coffin: “And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” Christ is the mediator of the new testament by means of his death, hanging on the cross. Redemption is the redeeming, and he died for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament.

Who was under the first testament? Israel. So those Christ redeemed are those who were under the law, the called who receive the promise of eternal inheritance: the heirs.

“And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father. Wherefore thou art no more a servant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.” When Christ died we were no longer servants but sons of the Father, and heirs through his Son.

precepts.text: Almost all things are by the law purged with blood. Almost, not all, so stop saying blood sacrifice; the heathen will come with that. Leviticus 5:11-12: if he be not able to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering, with no oil or frankincense, and the priest burns a memorial of it. Sirach 35:1-3: he that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough; he that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; to depart from wickedness is pleasing to the Lord, and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation. Israel never got there; it thought it could sin and sacrifice endlessly, and the Lord said enough.
precepts.point: Ye observe days, and months, and times, and years; I am afraid of you, lest I have bestowed upon you labour in vain. Colossians 2:16: let no man judge you in meat or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days, which are a shadow of things to come, but the body is of Christ. Ezekiel 45:17 answers both: it was the prince's part to give burnt offerings, meat offerings, and drink offerings in the feasts, the new moons, the sabbaths, and all solemnities, to make reconciliation for the house of Israel. On each of those days you had to sacrifice, and the Pharisees, whose bread and butter was people bringing animals, were trying to win the churches back to temple law, saying to hell with what Christ did. If you need an animal, you are condemned, because the temple would be destroyed.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
“And almost all things are by the law purged with blood”. Almost, not all. So be mindful of always saying blood sacrifice, because the heathen are going to come with that. Not every sin offering was blood, because some among us were poor and could not bring a blood sacrifice.

Leviticus shows it: “But if he be not able to bring two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, then he that sinned shall bring for his offering the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil upon it, neither shall he put any frankincense thereon: for it is a sin offering.” The priest took his handful of it as a memorial and burned it on the altar.

And the main example was obedience: “He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering. He that requiteth a good turn offereth fine flour; and he that giveth alms sacrificeth praise. To depart from wickedness is a thing pleasing to the Lord; and to forsake unrighteousness is a propitiation.” A propitiation is reconciliation. When you depart from sin and keep God's commandments, that is sacrifice enough.

Israel never got there. Israel thought, I can sin all I want and sacrifice all I want, and I'm good. We were children under the schoolmaster, sacrificing and sinning again, going into slavery and out and back again. The Lord said enough of that, and sent his Son. That is why turning back to the weak and beggarly elements is turning back to bondage.

precepts.text: Meats, drinks and divers washings were carnal ordinances until the time of reformation.
precepts.point: It is impossible to renew to repentance those who fall away after being enlightened.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Rome taught that in order to be saved you must be water baptized. Hebrews 6 answers it: “Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection”. The principles of the doctrine of Christ are animal sacrifice. The principle goes to the beginning; that is how we got forgiveness of sin at first. And among the things we must leave, Paul names “the doctrine of baptisms”.

Hebrews 9:10 shows what those washings were: “Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation”. Divers washings are carnal ordinances. They were imposed only until the time of reformation, and then they were to end.

So when Hebrews 6:1 says leave the principles, it means leave the meats, the drinks and the divers washings with the animal sacrifices. We did not get perfection in animal sacrifice, and water baptism belongs with those carnal ordinances.

precepts.text: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation. Carnal ordinances. So these are the commandments contained in ordinances. The law of sacrifice. That was the enmity. That was the wall of partition between them.
precepts.point: What are those commandments that are contained in ordinances? What is that talking about?

note.label: Christians Don't Understand Ephesians 2

precepts.why:
Ephesians 2:14 speaks of “the middle wall of partition between us.” What is that wall? The next verse explains it: “Having abolished in his flesh the enmity, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances.” A Christian’s head just blew off. They do not know what that is talking about. What are those commandments contained in ordinances?

Hebrews tells us. The tabernacle service “was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.”

Carnal ordinances. These are the commandments contained in ordinances: the law of sacrifice. That was the enmity, and that was the wall of partition between the two kingdoms. It was imposed only until the time of reformation, and Christ abolished it in his flesh, so that there is no more fighting over where and how to sacrifice.

precepts.text: Into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people.
precepts.point: The priests went always into the first tabernacle accomplishing the service of God, but into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood. Christ offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, so the day of atonement is still kept by afflicting the soul and doing no work, but without the animal sacrifice, because Christ took the place of the animal.

note.label: Exodus 30: The Altar of Incense and the Holy Anointing Oil

precepts.why:
“Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people”.

That once every year is the day of atonement, when Aaron made atonement upon the horns of the altar with the blood of the sin offering of atonements, for himself, for the priests and for all the people. The high priest went in alone, and not without blood.

precepts.text: Into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people; even the priests sinned.
precepts.point: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God. Christ took away the first covenant to establish the second, and we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all. Men had been sacrificing since the days of Adam; when Christ came, one sacrifice ended it, because that lamb had no blemish. The law of sacrifice was always temporary, a shadow of good things to come, and the good thing that came was Christ.

note.label: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering for Sins of Ignorance

precepts.why:
Even the priest that is anointed committed sin, according to the sin of the people, and had to bring a young bullock without blemish unto the Lord for a sin offering. Hebrews shows the order of the service: “the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people”.

Not without blood, offered for himself and for the errors of the people: the high priest had sins of his own to atone for before the people’s. The sin offering of Leviticus 4 covered the anointed priest as well as the soul that sinned through ignorance.

precepts.text: The gifts and sacrifices were a figure for the time then present, carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation; Christ being come stands in place of them.
precepts.point: The meat offerings and drink offerings and carnal ordinances were a figure for the time then present, imposed until the time of reformation; they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. But Christ being come, an high priest of good things to come, Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
The offerings of Pentecost, the lambs, the bullock, the rams, the kid of the goats, the meat offering and the drink offerings, were “a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience.”

They “stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.” They had a set time.

“But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands”: Christ is now in place of all those oblations and sacrifices. The holy convocation of Pentecost stands, a statute for ever; the sacrifices are fulfilled in him.

precepts.text: Into the second tabernacle went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and the errors of the people, the Holy Ghost signifying that the way into the holiest was not yet made manifest, standing only in meats and drinks and divers washings, carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation, which is the coming of Christ.
precepts.point: Hiram makes the lavers, shovels, and basins, and finishes all the work he made for Solomon for the house of the Lord: the two pillars, the two bowls of the chapters, the two networks, four hundred pomegranates, the ten bases and their lavers, the one sea, and the twelve oxen under it. All these vessels are of bright brass, cast in the plain of Jordan in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarthan, left unweighed because they were exceeding many.

note.label: 1 Kings 7: Solomon's House and the Brass Work of the Temple

precepts.why:
“But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people: The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing”.

It was “a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.” The time of reformation is the coming of Christ.

That is what all Hiram’s bright brass served: the lavers, the shovels, the basons, the ten bases and ten lavers, the one sea on twelve oxen. They were for the washings and the sacrifices of that service, vessels so many “Solomon left all the vessels unweighed”, all belonging to the carnal ordinances that stood until Christ came.

precepts.text: He is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament.
precepts.point: The rending of the veil is a sign. What stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.

note.label: Luke 23: The Trial, the Crucifixion, and the Burial

precepts.why:
At the ninth hour the sun was darkened “and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.” The rending of the veil is a sign: what stood between the holy place and the holiest was opened, and the sacrificial service under the first testament was coming to its end.

Hebrews gives the meaning. “How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?” His blood does what the blood of the sacrifices did, and more.

“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.” His death redeems the transgressions that were under the first testament. So when he gave up the ghost and the veil was torn, the offering had been made; the sacrifices of the first testament had come to their end and the new testament had its mediator.

precepts.text: The Holy Ghost signified that the way into the holiest was not yet made manifest while the first tabernacle stood; the gifts and sacrifices could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience.
precepts.point: As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
“The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience”.

While the first tabernacle stood, the way into the holiest was not yet made manifest. The gifts and sacrifices offered there were a figure for the time then present, and they could not make him that did the service perfect as pertaining to the conscience. That is why they had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice: Moses' sacrifices could not forgive sins the way Christ can. Being baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus is believing that.

precepts.text: Moses sprinkled the book and the people with blood, and almost all things are by the law purged with blood; without shedding of blood there is no remission, so under the first covenant only the blood of animals brought forgiveness.
precepts.point: As yet the Holy Ghost was fallen upon none of them; only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They first had to believe in Christ in the place of animal sacrifice, believing that Christ could forgive sins when Moses' sacrifices could not. The subject matter of that day was the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, which is why the apostles keep saying to repent and believe in his name.

note.label: Acts 8: The Word Scattered Abroad, and the Baptism unto the Conscience

precepts.why:
Under the first covenant, forgiveness came only by the blood of animals. “when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people, Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.” He sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry too, “And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.”

Without shedding of blood there is no remission. So being baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus for the remission of sins is believing on Christ in the place of the blood of calves and goats. That is the law and animal sacrifice versus the name of Jesus Christ, the subject matter of that whole day.

precepts.text: The gifts and sacrifices stood only in meats, drinks, and carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation, which is Christ.
precepts.point: Christ is the peace between the two kingdoms, having broken down the middle wall of partition, which was animal sacrifice, the ordinances the north was estranged from. By abolishing that carnal ordinance in his flesh, he made the two one, so Ephraim is no longer a stranger but a fellow citizen.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
The gifts and sacrifices were “a figure for the time then present”, which “stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.”

The time of reformation is Christ. The ordinances that kept Judah apart from the unclean were imposed only until he came, and that is why God showed Peter not to call any man common or unclean.

precepts.text: He is mediator of the new testament by means of death for the redemption of transgressions under the first testament.
precepts.point: Only Israel could receive remission because sin is the transgression of the law, and the law and the first testament of animal sacrifice were given to Israel alone. Christ's blood was shed for the many of the nation of Israel who were under that first covenant.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.”

Christ died for the transgressions that were under the first testament. The first testament of animal sacrifice was given to Israel alone, so the redemption is for those who were under it.

precepts.point: That is why Christ is called the end of the law (of sacrifice) to them that believe. Ephesians 2:14-16 shows Christ broke down the middle wall of partition between the two kingdoms, abolishing in his flesh the enmity (the law of commandments contained in ordinances, meaning the sacrificial laws), making of twain one new man.

note.label: Galatians 2: The Council at Jerusalem and Justification by Faith

precepts.why:
“the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience; Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.”

The gifts and sacrifices were carnal ordinances imposed only until the time of reformation. To compel Titus to be circumcised and return to animal sacrifice was to go back to what could not make a man perfect, and to shut out the northern kingdom that had no access to it. “It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these”: the things done on earth are based on things in the heavens, but the things in the heavens are better and pure.

“For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands”: Christ could not go into the temple; he was not a Levite. “Which are the figures of the true”: symbols of the true sanctuary, the true holy of holies. “But into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us.” So thy will be done in earth as it is in heaven: the temple John saw opened in heaven is the true one.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 1 A Visit From The Lord

precepts.why:
He is the one that washed us from our own wickedness. It is his blood that washes us from our sin. Our sins are not washed away because of our quote unquote good works; our sins are washed away because of the sacrifice Christ gave for us.

“How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works” The dead works is the breaking of the commandments. “to serve the living God?” Right now, because he purged us from our dead works, our breaking of God's law, now we can serve the living God. How so? By keeping the commandments. That is through Christ's blood.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 12 Red Dragon, Red Herring

The ones who left out of this truth all had testimonies, and they changed their doctrines. When a man turns from his righteous way, the Most High will not remember his righteousness. Your testimony is of no force while you’re alive.
